answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a orchard as the anchor of the cost.
